rule_metadata.description: The complete or incomplete merging of a Noon Sakinah or Tanween into a succeeding letter from the Yanmu (يَنْمُو) group, accompanied by a 2-count nasal resonance.

theoretical_foundation.linguistic_definition: Idgham literally means insertion or merging (إِدْخَالُ شَيْءٍ فِي شَيْءٍ). Ghunnah is a nasal resonance originating from the Khayshum (nasal cavity).
theoretical_foundation.applied_tajweed_definition: Meeting of a non-vowelled Noon (نْ) or Tanween with one of the four letters of 'Yanmu' (ي, ن, م, و) across two separate words, causing the first sound to merge into the second with a held 2-count nasal hum.

trigger_letters.name: Ya
trigger_letters.reason: The nasal Ghunnah attribute remains while the letter Noon merges.

trigger_letters.name: Noon
trigger_letters.reason: The first Noon merges fully into the second vowelled Noon with Tashdeed.

trigger_letters.name: Meem
trigger_letters.reason: The Noon converts and merges fully into the Meem with Tashdeed.

trigger_letters.name: Waw
trigger_letters.reason: The nasal Ghunnah attribute remains while the letter Noon merges.

theoretical_foundation.duration_rules: The nasalization (Ghunnah) must be held precisely for 2 counts (Harakat) at a steady tempo.

critical_exception_izhar_mutlaq.condition: If a Noon Sakinah and one of the Yanmu letters meet inside a SINGLE word, Idgham is STRICTLY FORBIDDEN. It must be pronounced clearly (Izhar).
